subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What should the canonical inbound-media isolation boundary be across agents and channels: account-scoped, agent/session-scoped, tenant-aware, or explicit-share based?
rationale: The current issue is security-sensitive and a narrow account-subdir patch would set a durable media-reference and sharing contract without clear maintainer intent.

options.title: Define scoped contract first
options.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation touches storage and staging paths.

options.title: Limit to account scoping
options.body: Implement the lower-friction account-based directory model, accepting that non-1:1 account-to-agent and tenant-sharing cases may need follow-up.

options.title: Defer broad core change
options.body: Keep only channel-specific slices open until a maintainer sponsors the cross-channel core media-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Define scoped contract first
recommendation.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation touches storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent blame on the central media/staging files and already reviewed this issue as the broad tracker.
